65: Uninstall from the currently selected ship(s) to cargo if there is space or to storage if there isn't.
66: Hold Shift, Control, or Alt to uninstall 5, 20, or 500 outfits at once. Hold a combination of these keys for larger amounts.
67: Transfer the outfit from planetary storage to cargo if possible. Otherwise, buy it from the outfitter.
68: Hold Shift, Control, or Alt to move 5, 20, or 500 outfits at once. Hold a combination of these keys for larger amounts.
69: Move the outfit from cargo, the currently selected ship(s), or the outfitter into planetary storage, in that order.
70: Hold Shift, Control, or Alt to store 5, 20, or 500 outfits at once. Hold a combination of these keys for larger amounts.
72: Hold Shift, Control, or Alt to buy 5, 20, or 500 ships at once. Hold a combination of these keys for larger amounts.
73: Sell the selected ships and their outfits.
74: Sell the hulls of the selected ships, but retain the outfits in storage.
75: Price the ship itself would sell for without any outfits installed.
76: Price that all this ship's outfits would sell for.
77: Energy and heat generated per second when this ship is idle, i.e. not firing weapons, moving, or using any other systems.
78: Energy consumed and heat generated per second when this ship is turning and thrusting. Includes the cost of using an afterburner if one is installed, or uses the cost of using reverse thrust if that is greater than the cost of forward thrust. This is in addition to the "idle" amount.
79: Energy consumed and heat generated per second when this ship is thrusting. This is in addition to the "idle" amount.
80: Energy consumed and heat generated per second when this ship is using reverse thrusters. This is in addition to the "idle" amount.
81: Energy consumed and heat generated per second when this ship is using its afterburner. This is in addition to the "idle" amount.
82: Energy consumed and heat generated per second when this ship is turning. This is in addition to the "idle" amount.
83: Energy consumed and heat generated per second when this ship is firing all its weapons. This is in addition to the "idle" amount. Note that weapons may consume or generate more energy or heat than this at the moment they fire, and this is the average value over time.
84: Energy consumed and heat generated per second when this ship is recharging shields and repairing its hull at the same time. This is in addition to the "idle" amount.
85: Energy consumed and heat generated per second when this ship is repairing its hull. This is in addition to the "idle" amount.
86: Energy consumed and heat generated per second when this ship is recharging its shields. This is in addition to the "idle" amount.
87: The sum of the energy consumed and heat generated per second from the above energy and heat values. Represents the worst case scenario when all possible systems are active at once.
88: Energy capacity allows a ship to temporarily draw more energy than it produces, and can be increased by installing batteries.
89: Heat capacity is the highest your heat generation can be without eventually causing your ship to overheat, and is influenced by the mass of the ship. If the "net change" value for heat is greater than this value, then the ship can overheat itself. Weapons with high firing heat per shot can cause you to become overheated even if "net change" is below heat capacity.
90: This ship lacks energy storage. Therefore, this is the greatest amount of energy that can be drawn by any of this ship's systems in a single instant, such as the energy required for a single shot of a weapon. Systems that require more than this amount of energy to activate will be unusable.
91: Weapons that are fixed in place (firing in the direction your ship is pointed) and that require no ammunition.
92: Weapons that can fire in any direction and will track your currently selected target.
93: Weapons that require ammunition (which must be purchased separately).
94: Outfits that serve as ammunition for other weapons. To fire this ammunition, you need a launcher of the appropriate type.
95: Outfits that occupy general space, not the space set aside for engines or weapons.
96: Outfits that either supply energy, or store the energy that is generated.
